title: Customer priority lanes & burst-credit wizard for Dedicated capacity intake
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers ask for predictable throughput SLAs but we lack a lightweight, consistent way to translate workload patterns into reservation recommendations and scaling rules. Current intake is manual, inconsistent across AE/SEs, and leads to over-provisioning, unpredictable fallbacks, and long negotiation cycles.

Goal: Deliver a self-service 'Priority Lane & Burst-Credit' intake wizard for Dedicated customers that maps customer workload fingerprints (latency SLO, steady-state qps, burst profile, diurnal patterns) to a recommended lane (reserved, hybrid-burst, or on-demand), suggested compute class (GPU family/quantization profile), and a burst-credit budget with time-of-day shaping. The wizard should generate a machine-readable SLA proposal and a small set of actionable defaults for infra (autoscale thresholds, cooldowns, pre-warm windows) that reduce manual triage and speed onboarding.

Non-goals: Full automated billing/contract creation and replacing enterprise sales approvals. Deep model re-architecture or runtime kernel changes are out of scope for this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Wizard UI prototype linked in Confluence with step-by-step intake flow and required customer inputs
Backend recommendation engine returning lane + compute_class + burst_credit (k tokens/min) with explainability fields for 90% of test synthetic workloads
Generated SLA proposal PDF/JSON that can be attached to customer intake and includes fallback rules and estimated monthly cost range
Playbook for AE/SE to override recommendations with rationale and audit log entries for traceability
Telemetry hooks added so recommendations can be validated against first 30 days of production usage (error budget burn, peak qps vs reserved)
